articles.title: Amazon refuses to film Jack Reacher plotline in deference to Orange Baboon
articles.description: #AlanRitchson had a great idea in mind for which #Reacher novel to adapt, but it was scrapped. Now, the star reveals why this happened: "Every season of Reacher so far has been great, and I understand that they may be avoiding the earlier novels due to their slightly less... pic.twitter.com/pioifheRn0 — ScreenRant (@screenrant) September 19, 2026 Amazon's Reacher series (starring Alan Ritchson) is a critical and viewer darling. Scoring 95/100 on Rotten Tomatoes the big white man with morals who kills people is in its 4th season. Jack Reacher is a character by Lee Childs with more than 30 novels beginning in 1997. Lee Childs has retired from writing after training his younger brother (now writing as Andrew Childs) to take on the series indefinitely. The Reacher books can be a bit confusing because they are not released in chronological order. The first book in 1997 is actually the 5th in chronological order. This does not prove as an obstacle to the production team because most books are standalone without time context. Childs/Ritchson/Amazon agreed to do a series based on Childs' second book - Die Trying but that idea was pulled prior to filming in deference to Trumpelstiltskin. This was not requested by the orange turd but a preemptive decision to avoid any ill will during late night Truth Social rants. Ritchson has confirmed this recently on social media. He writes that Die Trying is actually his favourite of all 30+ books. It was shelved as a season idea (not that anything was filmed but as a choice for a season out of all the books) because the climax focusses on Reacher killing through a white supremacy militia compound in Montana and ultimately taking out the bad guy(s). Amazon has renewed Reacher and it will continue. Just not with this book (honestly idk if it is Amazon or also the showrunners). Someone might get mad if their favourite group of people is targeted by their favourite 'real American' hero [no one associated with the books has claimed this (iirc) - just the mag/ha crowd]. Not getting into the actual human and his politics and the ultra white reactions. i read the books starting in 1997/8 and kept going for many years. i didn't actually know the books were still going. i always appreciated the violence bc growing up on batman/spiderman/superman/xmen cartoons people went to prison. but then they were the joker breaking out of prison every 5s. the bad guys killed people and the good guys didn't cross that 'line'. eventually you realise it's an empty threat. i want to say that i don't necessarily condone killing but like........the dichotomy of killing and morals is interesting. or was. idk. i just started the tv series tweet mods i cannot find the source for the photograph but the statement is written in the article linked

articles.title: Youth: Sharon Horgan’s comedy about dating at 50 is utterly hilarious
articles.description: The perils of ageing and the horrors of finding post-divorce romance are laid bare in the new show from the creator of Motherland. It’s humungously funny, and so acutely observed it’s painful Ageing has changed, hasn’t it? There’s a generation of middle-aged and perimenopausal elder millennials and xennials who refuse to do it. We’re young enough to be part of an online world that puts a premium on appearance, too old for such narcissistic self-branding to be achieved without unsustainable effort. Dating apps and social media connect people across generations, so it’s easy to become confused about how old we actually are. Here’s a tip: ask your knees. This brings us to Youth (from Monday 21 Sepptember, HBO Max), Sharon Horgan ���s dramedy about being 50. That perky title is a quip about the decade being known as “the youth of old age”. Horgan is Alex, a divorcee in her sandwich years, caring for teenage son Ruarí and ageing parents. There’s a lot going on in her life, and some doom. She’s falling forwards in a semi-successful career as a literary agent, getting back into dating under pressure. She needs someone to fall in love with her immediately, as she points out to her best friend. Not for romantic myth-making, but “so there’s a bit of time with the present version of me, before the ‘old me’ is here”. Continue reading...
